recipes.name: The 2 Dollar All American Breakfast | But Cheaper
ingredients: 2 lbs Yukon gold potatoes, peeled and quartered
2-3 Tbsp vegetable oil, plus more for drizzling
Kosher salt and fresh cracked black pepper
instructions: Peel and cut Yukon gold potatoes in halves or quarters. Place into a pot and add enough water to cover. Season generously with salt and place on the stove over medium-high heat and cook for 8 - 10 minutes or until soft. Drain your potatoes and let them sit and cool long enough until the outside is nice and dry.

Take a baking dish and generously coat the bottom with vegetable oil. Add in your potatoes and mash with the bottom of a cup. Cover them with an additional vegetable oil and toss to thoroughly coat. Season generously with salt and pepper, then place in an oven set to 425℉ for about 30 minutes; take them out once or twice to toss and turn.
For your pancakes, take a medium-sized bowl and add in flour, salt, granulated sugar, and baking powder. Whisk together until combined.
In a separate bowl, you’ll need whole milk, egg, and whisk in vegetable oil.
Next, whisk in your wet ingredients into your dry ingredients and continue mixing until you have a nice and even batter.

Heat a griddle or a non-stick pan over medium heat until nice and hot. Spray or grease with vegetable oil and pour in a heaping ¼ cups scoop of batter. Let that cook for about 2 minutes or until it’s halfway cooked and the bottom is a nice golden brown color.
Carefully flip and repeat on the other side. Repeat this whole process with your remaining batter.

For your meat, take about 1 lb of ground pork and add in your spices consisting of garlic powder, kosher salt, ground sage, red pepper flakes, and allspice. Mix it all together and thoroughly mix it in with the pork.
Form your pork into 2.5” wide discs that are about ½” thick.

To cook, simply heat up a very lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat. Place 4 patties in the pan at a time and sear for 2 - 3 minutes or until you get a nice deep brown crust. Flip and repeat on the other side.
To cook your eggs, heat up a non-stick pan over medium heat, adding just enough vegetable oil to coat the bottom. Add in your eggs about 2 - 3 at a time, avoiding them touching each other.
Once the egg whites are set enough to move around the pan, spoon the hot oil over them until fully cooked. Season with salt and pepper.
To assemble your breakfast, arrange in any orientation you’d like.
